overview.description: Canasta is a rummy-style partnership card game played with two 52-card decks plus 4 jokers (108 cards). Jokers and 2s are wild. Players form melds of 3+ cards of the same rank. A 'canasta' (meld of 7+ cards) earns powerful bonuses. The game originated in Uruguay in 1939 and became a worldwide phenomenon rivaling Contract Bridge in the 1950s. First partnership to 5000 points wins.

history.origins: Created c.1939 by Segundo Santos (lawyer) and Alberto Serrato (architect) at the Jockey Club of Montevideo, Uruguay. 'Canasta' means 'basket' in Spanish (referring to the discard basket).
timeline: 1939: Created at the Jockey Club of Montevideo, Uruguay.
1940s: Spreads to Argentina and South America.
1950: Rules standardized in North America (Classic Canasta).
1950s: Global crazeâ€”nearly displaces Contract Bridge in popularity.
Present: Two main variantsâ€”Classic Canasta (worldwide) and Modern American Canasta (North America).
history.evolution: The 1950 North American codification standardized 11-card deal, discard pile take mechanics, and canasta bonuses. Modern American Canasta (post-1960s) introduced more complex rules around wild cards, red/black threes distinctions, and going-out requirements.
history.cultural: A 1950s social phenomenon. Canasta clubs formed internationally. Associated with post-war prosperity and suburban social life in America and Europe.

setup.players: 4 in fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite). Variants for 2, 3, or 6.
setup.deck: 108 cards (2Ã—52-card packs + 4 Jokers). Jokers and 2s are wild.
setup.equipment: Two shuffled 52-card decks + 4 jokers. Score sheet.
setup.dealing: 11 cards each (Classic). Remainder is stock. Top card turned face-up to start discard pile (if red 3 or wild, bury and turn another).

rules.objective: Score 5000 points across multiple rounds by building melds, especially canastas (7-card melds).
rules.gameplay: Draw from stock or take discard pile (if top matches meld). Meld 3+ same rank; canasta = 7+ card meld. Jokers and 2s wild. Red 3s: lay face-up, draw replacement. Opening meld: 50/90/120 pts by team score. Go out: meld all, discard last. Target 5000.
keyRules: Initial meld minimum: 0-1499 pts (50 pts min), 1500-2999 pts (90 pts min), 3000+ pts (120 pts min).
Wild cards cannot form a meld by themselves.

strategy.basic: Race to your first canastaâ€”you cannot go out without one. Hoard wild cards; don't waste them on early small melds.
strategy.intermediate: Discard Pile Control: Never discard a card that gives your opponent an easy pile takeback. Coordinate with partner on which ranks to pursueâ€”don't overlap efforts.
strategy.advanced: Freeze the Pile: Discard a wild card (freezing) when opponents are about to take a large pile. Timing of going out is crucialâ€”go out when you maximize your card-point lead and prevent opponent's canastas.
tips: Red threes are pure bonus pointsâ€”lay them immediately and draw.
In the late game, use wild cards to complete your canasta quickly and go out.

list.name: Modern American Canasta

list.name: Samba
list.description: 3 decks. Allows sequence melds (same suit runs). Samba = 7-card run bonus. Target 10000 pts.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Samba uses three decks and sequence melds; engine overrides for deck count and meld types not yet added.

list.name: Hand and Foot
list.description: Each player gets 2 sets of cards (the Hand and the Foot). Foot is picked up when Hand is exhausted.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Hand and Foot two-pile structure and pickup rules are not yet modeled as engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Melds when possible. Doesn't optimize discard pile control. Ignores partner coordination.
difficulty.medium: Knows initial meld minimum. Basic pile freeze detection. Coordinates to avoid competing on same ranks.
difficulty.hard: Sophisticated discard pile management. Optimal wild card allocation. Precise going-out timing. Tracks freeze state and opponent's likely melds from discards.

considerations: Initial meld minimum varies dynamically by current score.
Wild card economy (Jokers=50pts, 2s=20ptsâ€”very costly to misuse).

ante.reason: Canasta is a meld game; no betting or antes.

deal.description: Deal 11 cards to each player. Turn one card face up to start discard pile (if red 3 or wild, bury and turn another). Remainder is stock.

reveal_market.reason: No market; draw from stock or take discard pile.

buy_market.reason: No market purchase; rummy draw and discard only.

buy_stock.reason: No stock purchase; draw from stock or take discard pile.

fold.reason: No folding; partnership meld game to 5000 points.

check.reason: No betting; score by melds and canastas only.

call.reason: No betting or calling; draw-meld-discard only.

bet.reason: No betting; points from melds and going out.

raise.reason: No betting or raising; rummy-style play only.

declare.reason: No declarations; meld and discard in turn.

reveal_hand.reason: No showdown; game ends when a team goes out.

award_pot.reason: No pot; partnership score from melds and bonuses.

play_card.reason: Rummy game; use draw, meld, and discard not play to tricks.

draw.description: Draw one card from the top of the stock, or take the entire discard pile if the top card matches a meld you can add to.
draw.constraints: One draw per turn; must draw before meld or discard.

discard.description: Discard card(s) to the designated discard zone.
discard.constraints: Allowed only when discard timing and count rules permit.

pass.reason: No pass; must draw then meld and/or discard each turn.

bid.reason: No bidding; fixed partnerships and target score.

meld.description: Lay down a valid meld combination.
meld.constraints: Allowed only in phases that list this action as legal.

go_out.reason: Going out is by melding all and discarding last; no separate action.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

hero.title: CANASTA
hero.subtitle: The 1950s Card Phenomenon
hero.tagline: Build your melds. Complete your canastas. Go out first.

synthesis.shortDescription: Uruguay's 1939 card masterpiece that briefly threatened to dethrone Contract Bridge. Two partnerships race to 5000 points by building melds and completing 7-card canastas with a 108-card double deck.

prompts.human: You hold 3 natural 7s and a Joker. You can meld 7-7-7-Joker (4-card meld, 30+50+5+5+5=95 base points). Is your partnership's score above 1500? If so, your initial meld minimum is 90 pts. This meld qualifies! Go for it.

scoring.description: Card values + canasta bonuses + going out bonus.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to 5000 points across rounds.
